title: Document analysis engagement
summary: AnalystOS analyzes a counterparty's source documents and delivers a sealed report in which every figure is a verified quote or an independently recomputed calculation. Every step closes with real evidence - never a claim either side merely asserts.

steps.title: Accept the engagement scope and its acceptance criteria
steps.brief: Agree the question, the source documents in scope, and the acceptance criteria this delivery will be judged against (see analystos/l4/acceptance.py::CRITERIA, agreed before any work starts, not after). Closes on the client's attestation that the scope and criteria are what they asked for.

steps.title: Gather the source documents and record where each came from
steps.brief: Collect the documents the engagement needs and record their provenance. Never publishes the documents themselves - closes on the client's attestation that the sources used are the ones they provided, not on a URL (the data-pilot playbook's own reasoning: a manifest, never the raw data).

steps.title: Draft a cited report from verified facts only
steps.brief: Every figure is either a quote checked against the source or a calculation the software redoes itself; anything unproven is dropped before a reader sees it. Closes by actually calling the unauthenticated POST /api/v1/verify endpoint with the sealed bundle and getting a 200 back - proving the bundle is well-formed and processable, not merely that a report-shaped file exists.

steps.title: Recompute every calculation and refuse any figure that fails
steps.brief: The same POST /api/v1/verify call as the previous step, but this time the response body itself is the evidence: it must contain "content_checked":true, which is only true when verify_bundle actually re-checked every citation and calculation against the source text and found none of them unproven.

steps.title: Seal the report so a stranger can re-verify it offline
steps.brief: The delivered bundle's own digest, recorded as a shipped/1 entry once this repo's record plane (drafts/README.md, Track C) is live, so that sealing this specific delivery is itself a checkable, dated event - not only the seal inside the bundle.

steps.title: Hand over the report and log every question it raises
steps.brief: Deliver the sealed report through a signed, expiring link (POST /api/v1/links) and log every client question against it. Closes with that link as the evidence - a real https:// URL the client can open.
